issue.title: [opencode-zen-free] free flash models return finish_reason=tool_calls with an empty tool_calls array; tooling clients stall (GLM-5.3-flash-free, DeepSeek-V4.1-flash-free)
issue.body:
## Versions

- Magpie app: `0.1.1559` at time of the occurrences (occurrences spanned several same-day auto-updates on 2026-10-26). Latest at filing: `v0.1.1564` (2026-10-26) — **not yet confirmed whether this is fixed in 1562–1564**.
- Plugin: `@magpie-community/opencode-zen-free-auth@0.1.15` (latest as of 2026-10-25).

## Environment

- Provider: `opencode-zen-free` (OpenCode Zen free tier, `https://opencode.ai/inference/v1`), keyless (`public`).
- Models: `opencode-zen-free/glm-5.3-flash-free:max`, `opencode-zen-free/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free:max`.
- Client: Hermes Agent — OpenAI Chat Completions surface, streaming, loopback gateway `127.0.0.1:3425`, served through a Magpie weight-routing group.
- Context at failure: ~73K–131K prompt tokens (both models are catalogued with a 200K context, so this is within the window, not an overflow).

## Symptom

The client intermittently receives an assistant turn whose `finish_reason` is `tool_calls` but whose `tool_calls` array is empty and whose content is not usable. Hermes log line (verbatim):

```
finish_reason=tool_calls with empty tool_calls array (narration only) — re-prompting to emit the call (retry 1/3, model=group/hermes-route provider=custom)
```

Hermes must drop the turn and re-prompt. 11 occurrences in one session on 2026-10-26; zero on any other day. No data loss (the retry succeeds).

## Two observed sub-shapes (from the per-request log at `~/.config/magpie/routing/<date>.jsonl`)

### 1. Billed-but-empty (5 of 11)

`status: 200`, `out` = 42–160 completion tokens were billed, the reply arrived as a single chunk (`flow: 1`), with **no** `firstText` and **no** `firstReasoning` — i.e. the model produced output tokens but delivered nothing as text, reasoning, or a usable `tool_calls`. Same shape as #3327 ("the model wrote a tool call that the parser could not turn into one, so it dropped it; Magpie relays it as a finished turn"). Verbatim rows:

```json
{"time":"2026-10-26T10:00:07.190+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"glm-5.3-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":56,"flow":1,"ttft":4902,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"glm-5.3-flash-free","in":73910,"out":56}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":10,"tokens":77293,"effort":"xhigh"}}
{"time":"2026-10-26T10:04:44.383+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"glm-5.3-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":42,"flow":1,"ttft":2453,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"glm-5.3-flash-free","in":1807,"out":42,"cache_read":73984}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":12,"tokens":79209,"effort":"xhigh"}}
{"time":"2026-10-26T10:22:42.616+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"deepseek-v4.1-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":160,"flow":1,"ttft":1948,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"deepseek-v4.1-flash-free","in":164,"out":160,"cache_read":73472}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":11,"tokens":73148,"effort":"xhigh"}}
{"time":"2026-10-26T11:47:15.442+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"glm-5.3-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":96,"flow":1,"ttft":3796,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"glm-5.3-flash-free","in":2851,"out":96,"cache_read":101184}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":14,"tokens":106731,"effort":"xhigh"}}
{"time":"2026-10-26T11:53:31.215+08:00","model":"group/hermes-route","served":"glm-5.3-flash-free","provider":"opencode-zen-free","status":200,"out":86,"flow":1,"ttft":3731,"usage":[{"provider":"opencode-zen-free","model":"glm-5.3-flash-free","in":1024,"out":86,"cache_read":125120}],"rule":{"n":0,"turn":16,"tokens":130910,"effort":"xhigh"}}
```

### 2. Narration + phantom finish flag (6 of 11)

Text/reasoning streams normally for 2–7s, yet the turn still ends with `finish_reason=tool_calls` and an empty `tool_calls` array — the model narrates an intended call but sets the flag without a payload. Matches #636 ("never emit finish_reason=tool_calls without delivering the corresponding calls").

## Repro attempt (negative) — the relay path is not systematically broken

Through the gateway, 12 clean non-streaming requests to both models with a forced tool call, at ~3K and ~60K context: **12/12** returned well-formed structured `tool_calls` with correct `id` (e.g. glm `62d6f350-…`, deepseek `call_00_…`). So the failures are intermittent and task-state-dependent (complex multi-turn sessions), not a consistent drop.

## What this is not

- Not a Hermes/client bug: the client detects the empty array and re-prompts correctly.
- Not a systematic gateway drop: proven by the 12/12 control probe above.

## Request

`emptyFails` / empty-turn retry is (per #3327) limited to Gemini and Code Assist. Extend it to Chat-surface free models — at minimum `opencode-zen-free/glm-5.3-flash-free` and `opencode-zen-free/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free` — so a reply with `finish_reason=tool_calls` and an empty array (or `out>0` with no content/tool_calls delivered) is retried / failed over instead of being relayed to the agent as a finished turn. Separately, when the `tool_calls` array is empty the `finish_reason` should be reported as `stop`, so a tooling client isn't misled into discarding a turn that actually just has narration.

## Related

- #3327 (GLM-5.3-flash tool turns end empty and are relayed as finished)
- #636 (`finish_reason=tool_calls` reported with no calls delivered)
- #2611 (empty-`id` streamed tool calls relayed as-is — related empty-tool-call relay class)

comments.body:
Took #3684. Branch: `fix/r25-empty-tool-calls-finish` on [skygunner/magpie](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/r25-empty-tool-calls-finish), commit `91625dca0bb33ee696be639e659bdf4c8f1b6abd`, base `19253f67bca2310c32739a6eaac88546b3574dbc`.

## Root cause

`chatTidy` (streamed) and `chatWhole` (whole responses) only ever upgraded a `stop` finish to `tool_calls` when a choice delivered calls. The reverse never happened: an upstream that narrated a call and ended `finish_reason=tool_calls` with an empty, null or absent `tool_calls` array had the contradictory finish relayed as-is, and the streamed per-choice "called" state even recorded an absent/null/empty array as a call. This is the narration + phantom-finish sub-shape of the report (6 of 11 occurrences), matching the #636 class.

## Fix (3 files, +113/−4)

- `internal/gateway/chattidy.go`: a choice that delivered no calls now ends `stop` when the upstream ended `tool_calls`, streamed and whole. Streamed state is kept per choice; real native calls keep `tool_calls`, and calls parsed from text (textCallTidy, which runs after chatTidy) still end `tool_calls`. An unreadable `tool_calls` value is treated as unknown and left as it came.
- `internal/gateway/chattidy_phantom_finish_test.go` (new): regression through the real HTTP surface for streamed and whole replies, absent/null/empty/absent-field arrays, with and without tools offered; native and text-parsed calls keep their finish and arguments; per-choice finishes in one chunk follow their own calls.
- `docs/subsystems/gateway-routing.md`: documents the normalization and its limits.

## RED → GREEN

RED at the clean base (production untouched, only the new test present):

```
=== RUN   TestChatPhantomToolFinish/#00/stream
    chattidy_phantom_finish_test.go:29: finish "tool_calls", want stop; text "Checking." calls map[]
--- FAIL: TestChatPhantomToolFinish
--- FAIL: TestChatPhantomFinishPerChoice
FAIL    github.com/yetone/magpie/internal/gateway   0.153s
EXIT_CODE=1
```

GREEN at head (`GOTOOLCHAIN=go1.26.8 go test -race -shuffle=on -count=1 -run "TestChatPhantom|TestChatCallsEndToolCalls|TestTextWritten|TestChatTidy" -v ./internal/gateway`, exit 0, 3.397s).

Also run: `go vet ./...`, `go build ./...`, `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -tags nogui`, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build`, linux/windows `go vet`, `gofmt -l` (all exit 0). Full `internal/gateway -race`: one failure, `TestClaudeClientCacheAbsentUnchanged` (Claude Code client-cache prompt marks) — proven failing at the base with `chattidy.go` restored (exit 1), pre-existing and unrelated. gopls is not installed in this environment, so LSP diagnostics were not run; compile/vet/tests cover the change.

## Limits

- This corrects the finish flag only. It does not implement empty-turn retry/failover or any billing policy; the billed-but-empty sub-shape (5 of 11 occurrences, #3327's class, prior BLOCKED_ARCHITECTURE disposition) is not addressed and the issue stays open for it.
- No real upstream request was made against opencode-zen-free; the fixtures are the wire shapes from the report's log and prior tests, exercised through the gateway's real HTTP stack in a sandbox HOME.

I claimed this issue earlier for independent verification — now standing down: [@skygunner](https://github.com/skygunner)'s branch covers it. I verified his fix independently instead of opening my own. Verdict: **the mechanism is correct and every ring of his description checks out, but his branch predates #1475 and conflicts with one existing test when merged to the current tip** — needs a rebase plus an explicit decision on that test, so I'm handing the evidence to the maintainers instead of a full endorsement.

## Mechanism, ring by ring (read from the full diff of 91625dca)

| Claimed | In the diff | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A choice that delivered no calls ends `stop` when upstream ended `tool_calls`, streamed and whole | `chatTidy` adds `finish=="tool_calls" && !called → stop`; `chatWhole` adds `known && len(native)==0 → stop` | Yes — ablation-red below proves the phantom relay is the pre-fix behavior |
| Streamed state kept per choice | Uses the existing `t.called[choice]` map; `TestChatPhantomFinishPerChoice` pins two choices finishing in one chunk, in reverse order | Yes |
| Real native calls keep `tool_calls` | `chatWhole`'s upgrade now `known && len(native)>0`; the stream side keeps its `called` upgrade | Yes — `TestChatPhantomFinishKeepsRealCalls/native` (stream+whole) |
| Calls parsed from text (textCallTidy, after chatTidy) still end `tool_calls` | `chatTidy` downgrades first, then `textCallTidy` re-upgrades to `tool_calls` when it parses a block; on the whole side `wholeTextCalls` writes the calls before `chatWhole`'s downgrade runs | Yes — `text_parsed` stream+whole sub-tests pin exactly this ordering gap |
| Unreadable `tool_calls` value left as it came (unknown) | `chatWhole`: `known := !has \|\| decodeJSON(...)==nil`, unknown falls through both branches | Code is there; **no test fixture exercises a decode failure** — not verified |

Plus one change he didn't list separately: the streamed empty-array drop widens from `== "[]"` to *decodes as JSON and has no elements*, so `null` and `[ ]` are dropped before delivery and no longer recorded as a call in the per-choice "called" state.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| His new tests at the fix (my run, 3-way onto `upstream/main` `e17b6cefc`) | `TestChatPhantomToolFinish` 16 sub-runs (absent / `[]` / null / `[ ]` × with/without tools × stream/whole) PASS; `TestChatPhantomFinishKeepsRealCalls` (native/text-parsed × stream/whole) PASS; `TestChatPhantomFinishPerChoice` PASS; `TestChatCallsEndToolCalls` PASS |
| Ablation (his new tests kept, `chattidy.go` reverted to tip) | RED confirmed: all 8 streamed phantom sub-runs + `TestChatPhantomFinishPerChoice` FAIL with `finish "tool_calls", want stop`; keeps-real-calls stays green — the tests do catch the reported phantom finish |
| textCallTidy ordering boundary (chatTidy before text parsing) | Pinned by tests, both surfaces: stream (`chatTidy` downgrades, `textCallTidy` re-upgrades) and whole (`wholeTextCalls` before `chatWhole`'s downgrade) |
| Full package: `go test -tags nogui -timeout 25m ./internal/gateway/...` | One failure: `TestToolCallsFinishWithNoCallsStaysWhole` — **introduced by this fix's intent, not pre-existing** (green under ablation); every other test passes (~11.5 min) |
| gofmt / `go vet -tags nogui ./internal/gateway/` | clean / exit 0 |

**The blocker.** `TestToolCallsFinishWithNoCallsStaysWhole` (in `chat_call_name_test.go`, from #1475, commit `82ff88933`, landed 2026-10-31) pins the old behavior: a whole reply that came with no calls at all keeps its `tool_calls` finish as it came (`content:"Done."`, no calls → finish stays `tool_calls`). That is precisely the behavior #3684 asks to change. His branch is based on `19253f67b` (2026-10-26), five days before #1475 landed, so his full-package run couldn't see this test. Merged onto the current tip, the fix turns that test red (`finish "stop"`, wants `"tool_calls"`).

Resolving it is a decision I shouldn't make on the author's behalf: either the test's expectation moves to `stop` per #3684, or #1475's conservative "a reply that came with no calls keeps its finish" carve-out survives for content-only replies and the downgrade is scoped tighter. Either way it needs @skygunner to rebase onto a tip containing `82ff88933` and update the branch, or maintainer arbitration. (For the record, no upstream commit references #3684 yet, and his branch head hasn't moved — re-checked today.)

How I merged it for testing (throwaway tree, not pushed): kept #1475's switch and appended his downgrade as an `else if` on `!t.called[choice]`; merged his doc sentence into the rewritten gateway-routing bullet; reconciled the "(a reply that came with no calls keeps its finish)" wording that his change contradicts.

Not verified: a decode-failure fixture for the "unknown stays as it came" ring; any real opencode-zen-free traffic (same as the author — fixtures are the wire shapes from the report's log, through the real HTTP stack).

Branch: [skygunner/magpie `fix/r25-empty-tool-calls-finish`](https://github.com/skygunner/magpie/tree/fix/r25-empty-tool-calls-finish) (head `91625dca0bb33ee696be639e659bdf4c8f1b6abd`, base `19253f67bca2310c32739a6eaac88546b3574dbc`)

Thanks @Terryli246 for the report and @skygunner for the fix branch.

AI use: verification performed with AI assistance; all commands and outputs above were run and read locally.

Thanks @ggbdpq for finding the conflict. I checked the pinned main b1e8eb15 source: TestToolCallsFinishWithNoCallsStaysWhole still explicitly requires a whole reply with content "Done." and no delivered calls to retain finish_reason=tool_calls. That is the opposite of the normalization requested here and implemented by my older 91625dca branch; this is an intentional contract conflict, not an unrelated baseline failure.

Please treat that older branch as a proposal requiring reconciliation with #1475, not as ready to cherry-pick onto current main. I will not remove or skip the existing test to present a green result. The two behaviors need an explicit maintainer choice: preserve the upstream finish for content-only replies as #1475 currently specifies, or normalize it to stop when no calls were delivered as requested here, with the documentation and guard updated together.

The billed-but-empty retry/failover request is still outside that branch. No real opencode-zen-free traffic was run this round; this follow-up is based on the current source/test contract and your independent regression evidence. I have not published a second competing branch.

issue.title: [bug] Mistral's GLM-5.3-flash ends some tool turns empty (response_error: empty_response), and magpie hands them to the agent as finished turns

repository.name: magpie
repository.description: Every agent's model. One place. Codex on DeepSeek, Claude Code on Kimi, from the menu bar.

issue.body:
## Problem

With `mistral/zai-glm-5-3-flash`, OpenCode often stops in the middle of a task as if it were done. In each case the last reply has no text and no tool call and ends with `finish_reason: "stop"`, although Mistral billed output tokens for it. Mistral says why in the reply's last chunk: the model wrote a tool call that Mistral's own parser could not turn into one, so Mistral dropped it and flagged the reply as empty:

```text
data: {"id":"383e9d30c29f4b1f9a0aeea97e07b01f","object":"chat.completion.chunk","created":1792723771,"model":"zai-glm-5-3-flash","choices":[{"index":0,"delta":{"index":0,"content":""},"finish_reason":"stop","logprobs":null,"response_error":{"format_error":null,"content_validation":["empty_response"],"tool_calls_validation":[],"extra_tags":[]}}],"usage":{"prompt_tokens":53666,"total_tokens":53734,"completion_tokens":68,"prompt_tokens_details":{"cached_tokens":18432},"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":0}}}
```

That chunk, an empty role chunk before it and `[DONE]` are the whole stream. magpie relays it unchanged, so OpenCode takes the turn as finished and waits for the user; "Please continue" gets it going again.

The cause is on Mistral's side: the same request sent straight to api.mistral.ai fails the same way. But magpie already handles this kind of reply for Gemini (#667: a reply that said nothing is asked again), and `emptyFails` limits that to Gemini and Code Assist, so a Chat reply from Mistral isn't covered.

## Environment

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Magpie | 0.1.1328 (macOS app; also 0.1.1327) |
| OpenCode | 2.1.3 |
| Platform | macOS 27.0.1 / arm64 |
| Provider | `mistral` preset, `https://api.mistral.ai/v1` |
| Model | `mistral/zai-glm-5-3-flash` (variant `max`; `high` behaves the same) |

## How often

I captured one real OpenCode request, the one after which a session stopped (31 messages, 12 tools, about 54k prompt tokens; the expected next step is a `read` call), and replayed it 20 or more times per setting:

| Model | Route | Empty `stop` replies |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `zai-glm-5-3-flash` | magpie 0.1.1328 | 4/20 |
| `zai-glm-5-3-flash` | magpie 0.1.1327 | 4/37 |
| `zai-glm-5-3-flash` | direct to api.mistral.ai | 20/97 (streamed or not, effort `max` or `high`) |
| `zai-glm-5-3` | magpie and direct | 0/60 |

Every empty reply carries `"content_validation":["empty_response"]`, with 8 to 80 completion tokens. `usage.jsonl` logs them like an ordinary end: status 200, `"stop":"stop"`, `out` 15 to 43, `ttft_ms` null, no `err`, no `tries`.

In my OpenCode history, all five premature stops on Mistral are `zai-glm-5-3-flash` (in about 180 steps); none on `zai-glm-5-3` or `mistral-large-4-0`. Three of the five streamed some reasoning first and then ended the same way (usage log: e.g. `out` 321, `reasoning` 265, `first_text_ms` null, `stop`). I could only reproduce the plain empty kind in the replays.

## Expected result

A Chat reply from Mistral flagged `"content_validation":["empty_response"]` is asked again in place, as #667 does for Gemini, since the agent got nothing it can act on. The flag is Mistral's own, so it shouldn't catch a reply that is legitimately empty. In the replays above, asking again would usually have worked: 16 of the 20 tries through 0.1.1328 came back with a tool call.

## Notes

- Related: #2972 (a `length` reply that is all reasoning is handed to the agent as a success).
- Mistral's same field also reports the calls it did parse but got wrong, `"tool_calls_validation":["tool_bad_args_schema"]` or `["tool_bad_args_json"]`, with GLM's markup leaking into the arguments, e.g. `{"limit": 265, "offset</arg_key>4405</arg_value><arg_key>path": "/Users/infinitr0us/Desktopme.txt"}`. Those reach the agent as a failed tool call and the model retries, so they don't stop the run; mentioned only as context.
- Workaround: `mistral/zai-glm-5-3` instead of the flash model.

Not tried: other agents (Codex, Claude Code, Pi) with this model.
